title: One password, everywhere
brief: 18:05. A breach alert: a shop you once used has lost its customers' passwords. Yours was one of them, and you used it elsewhere.
insight: Attackers do not guess passwords. They take a leaked list and try every pair on every other site. It is called credential stuffing.
teaches: A breach at one site becomes a break in anywhere the same password was used
Give every account its own password: a password manager makes that effortless
Passkeys leave nothing to reuse or steal

value.label: Passkey on this computer: nothing to type, nothing to reuse

mail.subject: New sign in to your Spendhawk account
body: We noticed a new sign in to your Spendhawk account.
If this was not you, change your password now. Anyone with your password can see and submit expense claims.

headers.summary: A genuine alert from Spendhawk: someone signed in with your password from {{place}}.

mail.subject: Your email was found in the Kettlewren breach
body: The address s.rivera@veltrix-logistics.com appeared in a data breach at Kettlewren, an online shop, on 21 September.
Exposed: email addresses and passwords, stored with a weak hash that is easy to reverse.
If you used that password on any other site, change it there now. Attackers try leaked passwords everywhere.

effects.title: What does the leak reach?
body: Kettlewren lost your email address and password. You used that same password on other sites.

choices.label: Just the Kettlewren password. That is where the breach was.
Every account that used it, starting with anything for work
Nothing. My Veltrix password is different.

outcome.label: Left the leaked password in use elsewhere
outcome.what: The same password still opens Spendhawk and The Freight Ledger. Someone already used it on Spendhawk at 17:04.
outcome.ideal: changes every account that shared a leaked password.

card.title: The leak was already being tried
body: Within minutes of the leak, the pair was tried on other sites. Your Veltrix sign in held because that password is different. Spendhawk did not: someone signed in from {{place}}.
The fix is one password per site, which only works if a password manager remembers them for you.
card.ideal: changes the leaked password everywhere it was used.

outcome.label: Went after every account with that password
outcome.what: The breach was at Kettlewren, but the risk is everywhere the password worked.
outcome.ideal: treats a leaked password as leaked everywhere it was used.

fix.objective: Give every account that shared the password its own strong one.

hint.text: Open Vault. Every login marked Reused gets Make strong: Kettlewren, Spendhawk and The Freight Ledger.

outcome.label: No account shares a password any more
outcome.what: The leaked password opens nothing. Vault remembers the new ones, so you never have to.
outcome.ideal: uses a password manager so every account has its own password.

card.title: The leak opens nothing now
body: Every account that shared the leaked password has its own strong one, and the attacker in Spendhawk is locked out.
Nobody can remember a different strong password for every site. That is the job of a password manager. For the accounts that allow it, a passkey is better still.
card.ideal: keeps one password per site, in a password manager.

passkey.objective: Add a passkey to your Veltrix account.

hint.text: Account security, Sign in methods: turn on the passkey.

outcome.label: Turned on a passkey
outcome.what: A passkey cannot be reused, phished or leaked in someone else's breach.
outcome.ideal: uses passkeys wherever they are offered.
